text:
Detroit's season has a story it can't get away from. Dylan Larkin, the captain until this year, wants out, has refused to play until he's traded, and was suspended without pay in late October, and the Red Wings aren't naming a captain this season. The team on the ice has gone 0-4 since the Avalanche game that left Moritz Seider talking about frustration. Tuesday in St. Louis they lost 3-2, and the scoreline was kinder than the first 40 minutes.

Detroit actually scored first, Andrew Copp tipping in a Ben Chiarot shot with 13 seconds left in the first period. Then the second period opened and the Blues took the game in under two minutes. Pius Suter tied it 37 seconds in, his 100th career goal and 200th career point, and Justin Barron gave St. Louis the lead at 2:34 off a Robert Thomas feed, moving the Blues' win chance from 52% to 70%. Through two periods St. Louis had 2.2 expected goals (the quality of chances) to Detroit's 0.62. At even strength across the whole night it was 2.99 to 1.38.

The Red Wings pushed hard in the third, out-chancing St. Louis 2.2 to 1.02, but Joel Hofer was waiting. His biggest stop came on Viktor Arvidsson, a 28% chance, and he finished with 30 saves and 0.8 goals better than expected. Jimmy Snuggerud made it 3-1 with a deflection at 15:58, set up by Dylan Holloway and Thomas, which is the line the Blues' own coverage has been asking to see reunited. Holloway had seven shots and 1.26 expected goals on his own. Seider's slap shot with 1:14 left, a 5% chance, only made the last minute nervous.

John Gibson was fine in the Detroit net: three goals on 33 shots, a little better than expected. Lucas Raymond had two assists. By our replay of every shot, St. Louis deserved this 57% of the time, and that's about right.

The Blues snap a three-game winless run and have now beaten Detroit twice in eleven days. The Red Wings' problem is bigger than one night in St. Louis, and it won't get smaller until the Larkin standoff ends.
headline: Blues win the middle, Red Wings' slide hits four
